pyramid schemes , mlm schemes , ponzi schemes , lotteries , and pump-and-dump penny stock scams are all flavors of negative-sum investment scams . the common feature is that there is no activity that generates new wealth that could repay the money that investors put into the game . > >

> > in a negative-sum investment , the only flow of money into the system is what investors put in . some of that money flows out to the investors themselves , and some to the creators / operators or other parasites . > >

> > in such a game , at any moment the total amount of money that investors have got out is always less than what they have put in ; and the difference only increases as long as the game is " working " . that is , the average roi of investors is guaranteed to be negative . > >
> > the distinction between pyramids , mlms , ponzis etc is in the details of how the investors money is handled , and how they are attracted . > >

> > in such a game , at any moment the total amount of money that investors have got out is always less than what they have put in ; and the difference only increases as long as the game is " working " . that is , the average roi of investors is guaranteed to be negative . > >
> > the distinction between pyramids , mlms , ponzis etc is in the details of how the investors money is handled , and how they are attracted . > >

> > for example , in a lottery there is a phase when investors ( players ) put money down , , then an event where some of that money ( typically less than 50 % ) is given to a few random investors . investors are attracted by marketing among those who can't grasp probability theory . > >
